newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 6.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 6.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

AMSTERDAM - Unilever, one of the world's biggest advertisers, tells marketers to change fundamentally the way they promote goods and services or risk being swept away by today's empowered consumers. Morris Tabaksblat, chairman and CEO of Unilever, warns manufacturers and ad agencies to stop telling people what to buy and instead to work harder at finding out how to satisfy consumers who are well-informed, busy and jaded.

CHICAGO - Walt Disney Co. wants families to get out their cheque books and prepare to set sail. The company is running a TV campaign for the launch of the Disney Cruise Line in April 1998. "We've got to begin to build awareness before the major booking period begins," says Howard Pickett, vice president of marketing at Disney Cruise Lines.

CHICAGO - General Mills Inc., which has bought the Chex cereals brand, aims to rejuvenate sales with an estimated $25 million national advertising campaign designed to restore the brand's image as an all-family cereal.

AMSTERDAM - Many Western advertising agencies that have rushed to Asia to cash in on the world's fastest-growing consumer markets are making mistakes and hurting their prospects in the region, Sonyon Kim, worldwide president of the International Advertising Association says.

CHICAGO - Tokyo-based Bandai Co. Ltd., maker of the Tamagotchi, the original virtual reality pet, are scrambling to assemble advertising and line up licensing partners. The company has shipped 10 million units globally since Tamagotchi was launched last November.

NEW YORK - An advertising campaign launching the Sony videogame PlayStation won the top prize at this year's Effie awards recognizing effective marketing. The campaign was created by Omnicom's TBWA Chiat/Day of Venice, California.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

NEW YORK - Advertising on the Internet's World Wide Web will grow rapidly, reaching $2.46 billion by 2000 from an estimated $446.2 million this year, according to a report from media consultants Cowles/Simba Information.

AMSTERDAM - Harassed consumers fighting information overload will increasingly turn to trusted media brand names to filter and select news and information for them, Time Inc president and CEO Don Logan says. "I think we're seeing a flight to quality in information. And I believe that flight to quality will accelerate in the next few years," he says.

PARIS - French pay television company Canal Plus and Franco-German firm SECA file a complaint with the European Commission accusing Spain of breaching European trade rules. "By refusing to approve the decoders used by Canal Satelite Digital, the Spanish Telecommunications Market Commission has prevented the sale of decoders already marketed in other European countries," says Canal Plus.

NEW YORK - Several of America's biggest media companies settle a federal copyright lawsuit against TotalNews Inc. forbidding the tiny Internet company from displaying their Web sites with TotalNews ads.

AMSTERDAM - Fears that powerful global media groups will undermine cultural diversity are unfounded. James Schadt, chairman and CEO of Reader's Digest Association Inc, says there was no point in big media firms trying to market bland, homogenous material all around the world because it simply would not sell.
WASHINGTON - A consortium of industry groups and privacy advocates urge the U.S. government to strengthen the laws designed to protect privacy in the new digital age.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
JOHANNESBURG - Coca-Cola Co says it will invest $45 million to double its business in Mozambique over the next four years.

TEQUILA, Mexico - Mexico, recognized as the official home of tequila in Europe, will try to win a similar status in Asia and Africa. "We will look to achieve similar results in Africa and Asia ... where we expect in the short term to win recognition of our tequila," Carlos Orendain Hernandez, president of the Chamber of the Tequila Industry, says.

JOHANNESBURG - South African food group Del Monte says it expects a drop in its earnings at the half-way and full-year stages of the current year due to a restructuring and difficult trading conditions.

SAO PAULO - The Greenpeace organisation in Brazil says it has launched an environment-friendly credit card with Brazilian Banco Excel Economico which is almost entirely free of the polluting plastic PVC and which is biodegradeable.

TOKYO - A unit of Toshiba Corp says it will launch the industry's first flash memory voice recorder which can record up to one hour of sound. Toshiba Video Products Japan Co Ltd says the pocket-sized devices, to be introduced on July 16, are only one-third the weight of a microcasette recorder and sound can be recorded over.
PARIS - France's Pernod-Ricard is about to buy spirits company Larios of Spain from the Gonzales-Gallarza and Villavincencio families, according to newspaper reports.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
MOSCOW - Figures show that an average Russian knocks back half a half-litre bottle of vodka each day, but many are buying fake vodka rather than the genuine product say officials.

TOKYO - Yamaha Motor Co Ltd says it will sell a special, limited version of its electric power-assisted bicycle. The special version will offer additional features worth 10,000 yen ($86.25), including a powerful rear brake, light aluminium pedals and a special bamboo-like front basket, but the price, at 92,000 yen, will be only 4,200 yen more than standard models. Demand for electric power-assisted bicycles in Japan is expected to reach 200,000 units in 1997/98, up from 100,000 the year before, and is projected to reach 500,000 units by 2000, Yamaha says.

BEIJING - China witnessed fewer marriages and more divorces than usual last year, the China Daily says. Official statistics showed that 9.34 million couples registered their marriages in 1996 while 1.13 million couples split up in the courts or official marriage registration agencies. The number of Chinese marrying foreigners in 1996 rose to 47,227, up 7.2 percent from 1995.
